bib.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold

Four supplementary videos (MP4, Supplementary Videos 1–4, structure trajectories) are not downloaded: not a text format. The Reporting Summary is also printed in paper.pdf (p. 11).

figures.caption: Median Cα r.m.s.d.95 of AlphaFold (group G427, highlighted) and the top-15 CASP14 entries, 87 domains, with 95% confidence intervals of the median

overview.one_line: AlphaFold, a neural network that predicts 3D protein structure from sequence and MSAs, reached a median backbone accuracy of 0.96 Å r.m.s.d.95 in CASP14 against 2.8 Å for the next best method.
abstract: The paper presents a redesigned AlphaFold that predicts the 3D coordinates of all heavy atoms of a protein from its amino acid sequence and a multiple sequence alignment of homologues. It combines a trunk of 48 Evoformer blocks, which exchange information between an MSA representation and a pair representation, with a structure module that refines a rotation and translation for each residue.

The model is trained end to end on PDB structures, with auxiliary losses, a masked-MSA objective and self-distillation on about 350,000 Uniclust30 sequences. In the blind CASP14 assessment it reached a median Cα r.m.s.d.95 of 0.96 Å on 87 domains, and on a set of 3,144 recent PDB chains the overall median was 1.46 Å.

The paper also reports a per-residue confidence score (pLDDT), ablations of each component, and limits: accuracy drops when the median MSA depth is below about 30 sequences, and for chains whose shape depends mostly on contacts with other chains.

details.problem: Predicting the 3D structure a protein adopts from its amino acid sequence alone, at near-experimental (atomic) accuracy even when no similar structure is known.
details.idea: Treat structure prediction as a graph inference problem in 3D space, with a network that jointly embeds the MSA and residue-pair features and directly outputs atom coordinates. Physical and geometric constraints (triangle-based pair updates, an equivariant structure module) are built into the architecture, and the network is refined iteratively by recycling.
details.architecture: Two stages (Fig. 1e, Fig. 3). Trunk: 48 Evoformer blocks without shared weights, which update an Nseq × Nres MSA representation and an Nres × Nres pair representation (row-wise and column-wise gated self-attention, outer product mean, triangle multiplicative updates with outgoing and incoming edges, triangle self-attention around starting and ending node, transitions). Structure module: 8 blocks with shared weights, with invariant point attention (IPA) and an equivariant update of per-residue backbone frames (residue gas), side-chain χ angles, pLDDT and pTM heads. Whole-network recycling (three times in Fig. 1e). Loss: frame-aligned point error (FAPE) plus auxiliary losses.
details.input: Primary sequence, an MSA built with jackhmmer and HHBlits (UniRef90, BFD, Uniclust30, MGnify), and the 3D coordinates of a small number of homologous template structures where available.
details.training: Supervised on PDB structures with release date up to 30 April 2018 (PDB copy of 28 August 2019), chains sampled in inverse proportion to 40%-identity cluster size, cropped to 256 residues, batch size 128 on 128 TPU v3 cores, trained to convergence (around 10 million samples, about 1 week) then fine-tuned with 384-residue crops (about 4 days). Losses: FAPE, distogram, BERT-like masked-MSA, per-residue lDDT-Cα, side-chain, and a structure violation loss during fine-tuning. Final model trained with self-distillation on 355,993 Uniclust sequences predicted by an initial model (75% of samples from the predicted set, 25% from the PDB). Five models with different seeds, with or without templates; the best per target is chosen by predicted confidence.
details.datasets: CASP14 (87 protein domains, blind test, May–July 2020); a set of recent PDB chains released after 30 April 2018 (10,795 chains after filtering; 3,144 chains without close training templates for Fig. 2a; 2,261 chains for the ablations in Fig. 4a); ablations also on CASP14 domains.
details.cost: Parameter count: not reported in the main text. Training: about 1 week plus about 4 days of fine-tuning on 128 TPU v3 cores. Inference, single model on a V100 GPU, without ensembling: 0.6 min for 256 residues, 1.1 min for 384 residues, 2.1 h for 2,500 residues; with ensembling: 4.8 min, 9.2 min and 18 h (Methods, Inference regimen).
details.code: https://github.com/deepmind/alphafold: source code, trained weights and inference script under an open-source license (licence name not given in the paper).
details.figure: Fig. 1a (CASP14 accuracy, p. 2) and Fig. 1e (architecture, p. 2)

quotes.text: AlphaFold structures had a median backbone accuracy of 0.96 Å r.m.s.d.95 (Cα root-mean-square deviation at 95% residue coverage) (95% confidence interval = 0.85–1.16 Å) whereas the next best performing method had a median backbone accuracy of 2.8 Å r.m.s.d.95 (95% confidence interval = 2.7–4.0 Å) (measured on CASP domains; see Fig. 1a for backbone accuracy and Supplementary Fig. 14 for all-atom accuracy).

The key principle of the building block of the network—named Evoformer (Figs. 1e, 3a)—is to view the prediction of protein structures as a graph inference problem in 3D space in which the edges of the graph are defined by residues in proximity.
The model uses MSAs and the accuracy decreases substantially when the median alignment depth is less than around 30 sequences (see Fig. 5a for details).

open_points: Number of parameters of the network is not reported in the main text (not found in the Supplementary Information by text search either).
The licence name of the open-source code is not given in the paper (only "an open-source license").

The 0.96 Å figure is the median over CASP14 domains (n = 87); on full chains of recent PDB structures the overall median is 1.46 Å (Fig. 2a), a different dataset and a harder measure (the paper notes it is sensitive to domain packing).
